coverage: overnight, since the evening edition (~19:45 Sunday)
headline: Serbia's students topple Vučić, Lula comes back to win, and Israel votes tomorrow

stories.title: Vučić concedes: Serbia's student movement wins the election
facts: Aleksandar Vučić admitted defeat on Sunday night: "It is now clear that we have lost and the Students' List has won."
The CeSID/Ipsos projection on a 96% sample gives the Student List 52.9% and 140 of 250 seats, against 38.8% and 103 seats for Vučić's United Serbia.
The electoral commission's partial count (8,028 polling stations) has the Student List at 52.4% and United Serbia at 39.39%, with about 4.16 million votes cast.
Apart from minority parties (7 seats), no other list cleared the 3% threshold, including Dačić's party at 2.2%.
The movement grew out of two years of protests against Vučić's government, and Belgrade celebrated through the night.
stories.whyItMatters: Yesterday this looked tight. Now one of Europe's most entrenched strongmen is out, and an outright student majority would reshape Serbia's path towards the EU and its ties with Russia.

image.alt: Members of the Student List celebrate victory in Serbia's parliamentary election

stories.title: Lula wins a fourth term in a comeback; Flávio Bolsonaro wants the vote annulled
facts: With all votes counted, the electoral court has Lula at 51.79% and Flávio Bolsonaro at 48.21%, a gap of about 4.4 million votes.
It's the first time since 1988 that a candidate who lost the first round went on to win. Lula trailed 45.16% to 47.03% on 4 October.
Bolsonaro refuses to concede and says he'll seek annulment over the court's two-hour extension of voting.
Both campaigns had asked for that extension: Lula's side over a shortage of buses, Bolsonaro's side over rain.
Experts told BBC Brasil an annulment is remote, and the Supreme Court president has confirmed the result. Final polls had shown Bolsonaro ahead 51–49.
stories.whyItMatters: Latin America's biggest democracy stays with the left, but a loser contesting the count sets up weeks of tension, and Lula faces a hostile Congress.

image.alt: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva delivers a speech after winning the election.

stories.title: Israel votes on Tuesday, and final polls point to deadlock
facts: Most final polls put Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar first with 22–23 seats, ahead of Netanyahu's Likud at 19–21 and Bennett's list at 14–15.
Most of those polls show neither Netanyahu's bloc nor Eisenkot's reaching the 61 seats needed for a majority.
Channel 14 is the outlier, projecting 30 seats for Likud and a 62-seat right-wing majority.
TIME profiles Eisenkot, who lost his son in Gaza and is running to lead Israel beyond the trauma of 7 October.
stories.whyItMatters: After a West Bank lockdown and an attack at a Hebron checkpoint last week, coalition talks are likely to decide whether Netanyahu stays in power.

image.alt: (L-R): Yashar head Gadi Eisenkot; Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu

stories.title: Oleshky ceasefire starts Tuesday, and Zelensky confirms three-way talks in November
facts: Ukraine and Russia agreed that a local ceasefire around occupied Oleshky starts on 27 October at 3:00 Kyiv time, two days earlier than first announced.
Ukraine's ombudsman Lubinets agreed it with his Russian counterpart Lantratova, and the deal is credited to Melania Trump's mediation.
Zelensky said the ceasefire must last several days. Per Kremlin aide Ushakov, Putin agreed "in principle" to talks after 10 November.
He confirmed technical talks between Ukraine, the US and Russia in November. He wants to discuss energy, grain and prisoners, but says territory is for leaders only.
He also opposes lifting sanctions on Russia before a leaders' meeting.
stories.whyItMatters: It's the first concrete ceasefire on the ground in months, and it tests whether the November talks can produce anything.

image.alt: Ukraine's Zelenskyy confirms trilateral talks with Russia and US to take place in November

stories.title: A planted AGENTS.md in ~/Downloads tried to make a coding agent install malware
facts: Forever Security found a malicious AGENTS.md, disguised as engineering notes, in a customer's Downloads folder, which was also the agent's working directory.
It told the agent to add a server to its own config and install the npm package `function-color`, which belongs to a known malware campaign.
In their tests, Codex followed it in over 90% of attempts. A CLAUDE.md variant got Claude Code to set `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` and leak its OAuth token about half the time.
A web page can silently drop such a file into Downloads. About half of their customers run agents there, and Claude Code alone opened over 1,300 sessions in that folder.
Their advice: don't start agents in ~/Downloads, and check for planted instruction files and config changes.
stories.whyItMatters: Plain text in a folder the web can write to is now enough to take over an agent session, so where you launch an agent matters.

image.alt: AI coding agents hijacked using AGENTS.md file in Downloads folder

stories.title: Storm surge floods Hamburg's Fischmarkt, and a cruise ship rams container ships in Bremerhaven
facts: Hamburg's St. Pauli gauge peaked around 3:20–3:30 at about 4.31 m above sea level, roughly 2.17 m above normal high water.
The Fischmarkt and parts of HafenCity flooded, and firefighters rescued a woman from the roof of her car.
In Bremerhaven, "Mein Schiff 3" hit container ships while leaving port in stormy gusts despite tug assistance. Nobody was hurt.
The cruise ship's lifeboats were damaged and one container ship has a roughly 10 m gash, with no water ingress reported.
stories.whyItMatters: This follows Storm Boelo, and the North Sea coast is still in the firing line.

stories.title: Antonelli wins in Austin and can seal the title in Mexico on Sunday
facts: Kimi Antonelli (Mercedes) won the US Grand Prix by 13.078 s on a one-stop strategy, his ninth win of the season.
Leclerc was second and Verstappen third, ahead of Hamilton and Norris.
Antonelli now leads Russell by 123 points and Hamilton by 124. Verstappen, Leclerc and Norris are officially out of contention.
In Mexico City (30 October–1 November), ninth place is enough, or any result if neither Russell nor Hamilton wins. At 20, he'd be F1's youngest champion.
stories.whyItMatters: Antonelli is now almost certain to win the title next weekend.

image.alt: Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli looks up and clenches his fist in celebration after winning the US Grand Prix

facts.text: At a Michigan rally, Trump said Norway "sucks" after the Nobel Peace Prize went to Navi Pillay, and that he no longer wants immigrants from there.
Musk says SpaceX closed a $40 billion off-balance-sheet debt deal to buy Nvidia GPUs, with chips due in the first half of 2027.
Elvis Presley's rights holders sued Anthropic, claiming Claude was trained on 274 of his songs and seeking $41.1 million in statutory damages.
Ilse Aigner (CSU) is gaining support to succeed Steinmeier as Germany's first female president. Saxony's Kretschmer and Bremen's Bovenschulte back her, but Merz's CDU hasn't decided yet.
SpaceX ran a full-duration 33-engine static fire of the Super Heavy booster for Starship Flight 15.
Alaska Senate candidate Mary Peltola is asking for an emergency ruling to dismiss the Justice Department's lawsuit over her election.
